summary:
Echo Point is an end-to-end Wildfire Monitoring and Rapid Response System which connects Earth Observation data from space to on-the-ground. The core application is a Command Dashboard, written in Python using Streamlit and Folium libraries to receive near real time data on thermal anomalies from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors using the FIRMS API.

This dashboard is used to visualise hotspots of active fires using an interactive map. Once a high risk area has been selected, commands are automatically sent to the physical rover prototypes to investigate the area. The rovers have obstacle avoidance, flame sensors and water pumps to put out flames.

By beating the crucial golden hour, Echo Point solves the issue of not being able to contain wildfires quickly. High resolution satellite data combined with automatic physical scouting means quicker response times, keeping vulnerable communities safe and helping the emergency services fight fires before they become a catastrophe.
details:
Echo Point is a complete system that helps respond to emergencies from space to the ground. It uses a web application that brings together almost real-time data on active fires from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors. This data is shown on a single, interactive map, making it easy for users to compare current hotspots with historical data and spot unusual fire behavior. When a user chooses a high-risk fire area, the app figures out where the nearest rover station is and sends a wireless command to dispatch it. The rover then drives to the area on its own, using an ultrasonic sensor to avoid obstacles and a flame sensor to scan for heat. If it finds a fire, the rover stops and turns on a water pump to put out the flames, while also sending live updates back to the web dashboard. This system is designed to work quickly and efficiently, helping to prevent fires from getting out of control. By using a combination of satellite data and autonomous rovers, Echo Point provides a powerful tool for emergency responders to fight fires and keep people safe.

What benefits and intended impact does it have?

The main thing is to buy some time when a wildfire starts, especially during the first hour which is crucial. This is because firefighters are usually a few minutes away from where the fire initially breaks out; Echo Point.
